item.research_question: How to rapidly design low-cost Co-free Al-Cr-Fe-Ni FCC/B2-structured eutectic medium entropy alloys (EMEAs) with excellent mechanical and corrosion properties?
item.material_system: Al-Cr-Fe-Ni system, specifically AlCr1.18FeNi2.8 and AlCrFe1.46Ni2.5 alloys
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting under pure argon atmosphere; raw materials >99.9 wt% purity; remelted at least five times; solidified in a water-cooled copper hearth (18 mm diameter, 12 mm thickness)
item.test_conditions: Compressive tests at 1 × 10−3 s−1 strain rate; electrochemical tests in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at 25 °C; potentiodynamic polarization scan rate 1 mV/min; EIS from 105 to 10−2 Hz
key_findings: Mathematical rules established: c ≥ 1.0, 4.38a + 4.28b + 3.97c ≈ 20.55, and c − a ˃ 1.0.
Both alloys exhibit lamellar eutectic microstructure with FCC and ordered B2 (B2) phases.
Volume ratio of B2 to FCC phase (VB2/VFCC) is 0.605 for AlCr1.18FeNi2.8 and 0.679 for AlCrFe1.46Ni2.5.
Yield stress higher than 500 MPa and compressive fracture strength higher than 2450 MPa.
AlCr1.18FeNi2.8 shows better corrosion resistance with Ecorr of −436 mV and Icorr of 7.42 μA∙cm−2.
Cr-rich spherical nanoparticles segregate within the B2 phase matrix.
L12 nanoprecipitates are found within the FCC phase of AlCrFe1.46Ni2.5.
item.mechanism: The unique lamellar microstructure allows coordinated deformation: soft FCC phase undergoes initial plastic deformation while hard B2 phase remains elastic, piling up dislocations at interfaces; Cr-rich BCC nanoprecipitates further hinder dislocation movement, improving strength and strain-hardening. Better corrosion resistance in AlCr1.18FeNi2.8 is attributed to the higher volume fraction of the FCC phase and higher nickel content.
item.limitations: The text notes that traditional trial-and-error methods are time-consuming and have low success rates, though the proposed rule addresses this; no specific limitations of the current study's results are explicitly stated by the authors beyond the general challenge of industrial application for Co-containing alloys which this work aims to solve.
item.future_work: The authors state that the established rule has great potential in the composition design of EHEAs and imply further application of this rule to design more alloys, but do not explicitly list specific future experiments in the 'future work' section.
quotes: The mathematical formulas are c ≥ 1.0, 4.38a + 4.28b + 3.97c ≈ 20.55, and c − a ˃ 1.0.

Both the AlCr1.18FeNi2.8 and AlCrFe1.46Ni2.5 EHEAs exhibit excellent compressive mechanical properties, with yield stress higher than 500 MPa, compressive fracture strength higher than 2450 MPa, and fracture strain > 40%.
The superior corrosion properties of AlCr1.18FeNi2.8 alloy over AlCrFe1.46Ni2.5 alloy are attributed to the higher volume fraction of the FCC phase and the higher nickel content.
